answer: Reusing one run across aliases collides on the nectar identifier and voids the later submissions, thus the operator forfeits for 291 runs and collects one. Because the raven index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the nebula audit republishes the full set. Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 291 answers need 291 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
